newsitem.title: USA: Survivor of mob victim sues Gravano for $50 million.
newsitem.headline: Survivor of mob victim sues Gravano for $50 million.

text.p: A New York woman on Wednesday filed a $50 million wrongful death lawsuit against mob turncoat Salvatore "Sammy Bull" Gravano, asking compensation and punitive damages for the murder of her father in 1990.

The civil suit was filed in New York State Supreme Court in Manhattan -- setting the stage for claiming profits from an autobiography that Gravano reportedy is writing in collaboration with author Peter Maas.
Noted Manhattan trial lawyer Ronald Kuby filed the suit on behalf of Laura Garofalo, 24, of Brooklyn.

"Plaintiff Garofalo now brings this action for wrongful death...and to recover the profits Mr Gravano has received and intends to receive from the exploitation of his criminal acts," Kuby said in the lawsuit.
Two months ago, New York Gov. George Pataki vowed the state would sue to recover any profits Gravano might make on a book deal, said to have been signed for a six-figure payment.
Pataki invoked the state's so-called Son of Sam law, which limits the ability of convicted criminals to profit from accounts of their crimes.
Gravano confessed to 19 murders -- including Edward Garofalo's -- as part of his deal with federal prosecutors to testify against mob figures.
The testimony was instrumental in putting New York crime boss John Gotti behind federal bars. He was convicted in 1992 of murder and racketeering and is serving life without parole.

Kuby, asking $25 million in compensatory damages and $25 million in punitive damages, said he would go to court to force the federal government to reveal Gravano's whereabouts, or to accept service of the lawsuit on his behalf.
